Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the start of Zimbabwe's second innings. Brian Bennett and Ben Curran walk out to open the innings for the visitors. Bangladesh are starting with spin in the form of Taijul Islam. A slip and a short leg in place. Let's play...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

As for Zimbabwe, they ended the previous day on a high and were hopeful of limiting the lead, but missed chances in the field and their inexperience, especially in the spin department, proved costly. The ever-smiling debutant leggie, Vincent Masekesa, was the standout performer, claiming a memorable five-wicket haul but the rest struggled to take wickets or contain the runs. Now, they face an uphill task. While the pitch hasn’t shown demons yet, the hard new ball is expected to do a bit more, and it remains to be seen how the tourists handle that challenge. Back in a bit for Zimbabwe's reply.

Vincent Masekesa leads his team off the field, proudly holding the ball aloft after completing a five-wicket haul on debut. That brings an end to Bangladesh’s resistance, as they are bowled out with a significant lead of 217 runs. At the start of the day, with the lead at just 64, few would have expected it to stretch this far but Mehidy Hasan Miraz, with excellent support from the tail, made it possible. Earlier, it was Shadman Islam’s century that gave Bangladesh a solid platform, and despite a mid-innings stutter, they recovered well thanks to Mehidy and company.

OUT! STUMPED! Vincent Masekesa has a fifer! And finally Bangladesh's innings has come to an end. Tossed up, outside off, inviting the batter for the big one, Mehidy Hasan Miraz skips down the track to go for the big one, he misses as the ball turns away to beat his outside edge. Tafadzwa Tsiga does the rest. Bangladesh finish the first innings with a big lead of 217 runs!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the play to begin on Day 3. Craig Ervine and Co. head out to the centre. Blessing Muzarabani will get us going with the ball. Away we go...

Bangladesh do hold a 64-run lead, but with them set to bat last on a surface expected to deteriorate, their hopes rest on Mehidy Hasan Miraz to stretch that advantage. The second new ball is just four overs old, so Zimbabwe will be eyeing early inroads to tilt the balance their way in the morning. Stay tuned for all the action.

As for Zimbabwe, they looked bereft of ideas after the strong opening stand, but debutant leg-spinner Vincent Masekesa injected much-needed energy into their bowling effort. His timely breakthroughs in the third session hauled Zimbabwe back into the contest and ensured the lead didn’t spiral out of control.

Bangladesh appeared to be running away with the game across the first two sessions on Day 2, especially after bowling Zimbabwe out for 227 and then putting together a solid start with the bat. A century from opener Shadman Islam put the hosts in a strong position to build a substantial lead, but a mini-collapse in the final session stalled their charge.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks! It’s moving day in Chattogram, and after two days of compelling cricket, this Test remains delicately poised. The contest has already seen momentum swing both ways, and the remaining days promise no less drama.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, the Test is nicely poised with three days left. Zimbabwe’s strong effort has kept Bangladesh from taking full control. They will aim to wrap up the innings early on Day 3 and build a solid reply. For Bangladesh, Mehidy will be key in pushing the lead towards 100. Day 3 is called the 'moving day', and will the game shift decisively one way? We shall find out. Play on Day 3 will begin at 4 am GMT. Until then, take care and goodbye!

In the third session, Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim took Bangladesh into the lead, but Zimbabwe fought their way back through the debutant leggie, Vincent Masekesa. Mushfiqur’s run out while going for a risky single added to Bangladesh’s troubles as they slipped dramatically after being 259/3 at one stage.

Bangladesh needed just one ball to take the last Zimbabwe wicket, bowling them out for 227, with Taijul Islam taking six wickets. In response, openers Shadman Islam and Anamul Haque had a shaky start but settled in to put on a 118-run partnership. Shadman capitalised on the conditions and went on to score a ton. Zimbabwe struggled in the second session but ended it well with two quick wickets.

SESSION SUMMARY - 30 overs, 86 runs and 4 wickets. There’s something about the third session where the serenity of the day gives way to sudden drama. On Day 1, it was Bangladesh who came storming back, but on Day 2, it was Zimbabwe who turned the tide with a spirited fightback and will head into stumps as the slightly happier side. Yes, Bangladesh will be disappointed with the collapse, but they have managed to stretch their lead to 64 runs. Still, they will walk back to the dressing room, wondering what could have been after such a solid platform earlier in the day.

This wicket is offering some turn, but it’s slow turn, and not threatening enough. Zimbabwe spinners have to keep bowling in the right areas if they are to take some wickets. On the other hand, Bangladesh are possibly going to get the best phase of the match for batting, and they would want to take full advantage of it. Do join us for the post-Lunch session at 6.40 am GMT.

Initially, there was some help for the pacers, and the duo of Richard Ngarava and Blessing Muzarabani did create some problems. However, Shadman Islam and Anamul Haque both grinded it out in that tough phase, as the duo looked determined at the crease. Once the spinners came on, batting seemed to become easier, as both Bangladeshi openers kept the scoreboard ticking and were largely untroubled.

It took just one delivery today morning for Taijul Islam to wrap up the Zimbabwe innings, as the visitors were bowled out for 227.
